stories.title: CBSE plans assessment reforms for classes 10 and 12
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education is shifting its assessment framework to emphasize analytical reasoning and practical application. The reforms aim to reduce dependence on memorisation, aligning school-level examinations with the National Education Policy 2020. The board is moving away from traditional rote-based learning to competency-based education.

stories.title: Drishti IAS founder says graduation may lose relevance
stories.summary: Vikas Divyakirti told students that artificial intelligence is increasingly performing repetitive tasks like translation and legal research. He urged students to focus on human skills and aptitude rather than traditional degrees. Technology is changing the nature of work, and career choices should reflect that shift.

stories.title: Why every new AI decision is a mission decision - University Business
West Virginia students consider AI impact on future careers
stories.summary: As businesses integrate artificial intelligence, students in West Virginia are evaluating how the technology will reshape local industries. While the state economy relies on a unique mix of sectors, students are exploring technical training and career paths to prepare for a changing workplace landscape.

stories.title: Georgia Tech publishes classroom AI playbook
stories.summary: Georgia Tech has released a 278-page playbook featuring 67 faculty articles on integrating artificial intelligence into coursework. The resource offers instructor-tested experiments rather than a campuswide policy. The university used AI to help synthesise the collection of lessons on assessment design and classroom activities.

stories.title: Georgia Tech shares faculty experiments with classroom AI
stories.summary: Georgia Tech has compiled 67 articles from its seven colleges into an Academic AI Playbook. The collection details faculty experiences with generative AI, offering practical lessons on assessment and assignment design. The university aims to show educators what has been tried and what has been learned.

stories.title: Teachers debate AI regulation in the classroom
stories.summary: Educators are adjusting curriculums to address the potential for AI-assisted cheating. A Pew Research Center survey found 32 percent of K-12 teachers see an equal mix of benefit and harm in using AI tools. Schools remain divided on how to integrate the technology into daily instruction.

stories.title: Universities reconsider assessment in the age of AI
stories.summary: Indian universities are re-evaluating how they measure student understanding as AI tools become capable of writing code and essays. Institutions like IIM Ahmedabad and IISER Pune are experimenting with new assessment methods. Banning the technology is no longer considered a realistic option for preparing students.

stories.title: Cognitive science remains relevant as AI evolves
stories.summary: As artificial intelligence changes how society relates to work and health, educators are questioning how to prepare for rapid technological shifts. Developing skills for the current state of the art is increasingly insufficient, as those abilities risk becoming obsolete as technology moves forward.

stories.title: Fontana Unified students head to World Robot Olympiad
stories.summary: Fifteen students from the Fontana Unified School District will compete at the World Robot Olympiad in Puerto Rico this December. The six elementary and middle school teams qualified by designing and programming robots to solve problems. The competition hosts participants aged 8 to 22 globally.

stories.title: Pune student wins gold at Informatics Olympiad
stories.summary: Swasti Patil has become the first Indian to win a gold medal at the European Girls' Olympiad in Informatics. The student achieved the victory in May 2026 while pursuing an unschooled academic path. Her win marks a milestone for India in the field of competitive programming.

stories.title: Unschooled student secures historic informatics gold
stories.summary: Swasti Vitthal Patil won gold at the European Girls' Olympiad in Informatics in Italy, one year after taking bronze in Germany. Listed as unschooled in official records, she developed her academic journey outside of a traditional classroom. Her success is being noted for opening doors for others.

stories.title: Dhaka University student wins mathematics olympiad
stories.summary: Fatema Akhter of Dhaka University took first place at the National Undergraduate Women's Mathematics Olympiad. The event, held at the AF Mujibur Rahman Mathematics Bhaban, also saw students from Barisal University and Dhaka University secure second and third place respectively. The competition celebrates undergraduate mathematical achievement.

stories.title: Filipino students win awards at Dubai ROBOlution 2026
stories.summary: The University of Baguio was named overall champion at the ROBOlution 2026 competition held at BITS Pilani Dubai. Various other Philippine schools also received awards during the event in the United Arab Emirates. The competition highlights robotics achievements among students.

stories.title: Two MCHS students named Posse Scholarship finalists
stories.summary: Michigan City High School students Allysia Olmos and Kara Potts are finalists for the Posse Scholarship. The program identifies students with leadership potential for full-tuition awards at partner universities. The two finalists are currently being considered for scholarships to Purdue University.

stories.title: Two students from Ramgati qualify for English Olympiad Global Grand Finale - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
Bandarupalli Model School students win English competitions
stories.summary: Students from Bandarupalli Model School secured first prizes in TED-Ed Talk and English Olympiad competitions held in Mulugu. Class 10 student Patti Tanmayi won the speech category, while a Class 9 student took the top prize in the essay-writing competition. The events were hosted by ELTA.

stories.title: St George International School students win library awards
stories.summary: Students from St George International School in Karimnagar won multiple prizes during National Library Week celebrations. Winners placed in drawing, singing, rangoli and mehendi competitions hosted by the District Library Organisation. The school chairman congratulated the students on their district-level achievements.

stories.title: Bangladesh team to compete in 28th International Robot Olympiad
stories.summary: The 28th International Robot Olympiad will take place in Vienna from 12 to 16 January 2027. The Bangladesh team qualified following a national round in Dhaka that drew over 500 students. Participants in the national event secured 3 gold, 7 silver and 10 bronze medals.

stories.title: Ancient stone step may reveal name of lost Maya city
stories.summary: An ancient stone step recovered from Ocomtun has helped researchers identify a settlement now known as Minanbe. Epigrapher Octavio Esparza Olguin suggests the site may have been called Sakil. The findings were presented at a conference organised by the National Institute of Anthropology and History.

stories.title: Armenian student wins Russian AI Olympiad
stories.summary: Gurgen Bayburdyan, an 11th-grade student from Gyumri, took the top prize at the All-Russian Artificial Intelligence Olympiad in Moscow. Competing in the International Track against participants from Kazakhstan, Cyprus and Belarus, the 16-year-old outperformed his peers to secure the win.

stories.title: High school students win national prize for AI screening tool
stories.summary: Rohan Kundra and Neil Thakkar placed second in the American Lung Cancer Screening Initiative Innovation Challenge. Their project, LungFACTS, uses an AI patient navigator to help track screenings. More than 1,000 students entered the competition, with only 10 teams reaching the final round.

stories.title: Nuclear startup reaches $6 billion valuation
stories.summary: Isaiah Taylor, who left high school at 16, now leads Valar Atomics. The startup has reached a $6 billion valuation and secured $1 billion from Sequoia Capital. The company says its small modular nuclear reactors can power Nvidia AI processors to meet rising energy demands.

stories.title: Five Illinois scientists named among world's most influential
stories.summary: Five researchers from the College of Agricultural, Consumer and Environmental Sciences are among 12 University of Illinois faculty named to the 2026 Clarivate Analytics Highly Cited Researchers list. The list recognizes scientists whose work has been frequently cited by their peers over the last decade.

A guide to the primary to secondary school transition
stories.summary: Moving from primary to secondary school involves academic and social changes that may require time for children to settle in. Experts suggest that parents can assist by encouraging independence and organization. A positive transition can help build skills necessary for future post-secondary education.

stories.title: Singapore schools and the middle school terminology
stories.summary: Families moving to Singapore may find confusion in school terminology, as international and national systems use terms like middle school and lower secondary differently. At Global Indian International School, families with students in Grades 6 to 8 can consider the Cambridge Lower Secondary Programme.

stories.title: Flood safety and the risk of underestimating danger
stories.summary: Flooding is a leading cause of death during climate disasters. People often wade through floodwater to reach home, frequently underestimating the speed or power of the current. Many fail to spot underwater hazards that can cause them to trip and fall in dangerous conditions.

stories.title: Pharmacists urged to lead on diabetes screening
stories.summary: November is National Diabetes Month, with more than 40 million Americans living with the condition. Pharmacists are encouraged to use medication therapy management to screen for diabetes and educate patients on lifestyle modifications. The American Diabetes Association notes the importance of early action.

stories.title: Patchwork workshops used to support teacher identity
stories.summary: A study in BMC Medical Education suggests that collaborative patchwork workshops can help health professions educators reflect on their professional identity. While faculty development often focuses on instructional skills, researchers argue that arts-based approaches can address the personal dimensions of teaching roles.

stories.title: Options for students pursuing economics degrees
stories.summary: Students interested in economics can consider programs at Madras School of Economics, Christ University or Pondicherry University. These institutions offer various undergraduate and integrated degrees with focuses on quantitative finance, econometrics and corporate recruitment. Each school provides different campus environments and placement opportunities.

stories.title: IBS of Provence shares transition advice for families
stories.summary: Erica Prien, head of admissions at IBS of Provence, advises new international families to embrace the school community and build connections. The school aims to provide a supportive environment to help students and families feel at home during the transition period.

stories.title: Academia-industry collaboration key to tackling unemployment: UGC member - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
UGC Chairman calls for responsible, ethical use of AI in education - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
Chetana Education targets 1,000 schools for Olympiad
stories.summary: Chetana Education aims to bring 750 to 1,000 schools into its NextGen Olympiad next year. The first rollout reached over 175 schools and distributed 24,000 papers. The company reported a consolidated turnover of 65.63 crore rupees for the first half of the 2027 fiscal year.

stories.title: Lorestan University announces sports olympiad
stories.summary: The Physical Education Department of Lorestan University has announced an intra-university sports olympiad for students. The Student Affairs Vice-Presidency has invited registration for the upcoming event. Students are directed to consult the university's provided files and images for the registration process and the schedule of sports disciplines.

stories.title: Doha hosts spell bee season two finale
stories.summary: The Indian Women Welfare Organisation held the grand finale of its Spell Bee Season II in Doha on November 6. The competition drew 354 students to the preliminary round, with 24 finalists competing across four age categories to demonstrate their vocabulary, memory, and confidence.

stories.title: Birla Public School student wins three swimming medals
stories.summary: Natasha Padman, a Grade X student at Birla Public School in Doha, secured three medals at the CBSE National Girls Swimming Championship 2026 in Bhopal. She earned two silver medals and one bronze, alongside fourth-place finishes in two additional events. Her performance was cited as an inspiration to peers.

stories.title: SMR International School hosts Hindi drama competition
stories.summary: SMR International School in Safidon held its fifth Inter-House Hindi Drama Competition. Four houses performed plays addressing social issues through satire and humour. Sahayog Sadan secured first place, while individual awards were presented to students Yug and Vanshika for their acting performances during the event.

stories.title: Antonio Da Silva wins inter-school football match
stories.summary: Dr Antonio Da Silva High School defeated Rustomjee Cambridge International School 4-0 in a boys U-12 football match at Azad Maidan. Striker Arnav Rane scored two goals during the league match of the Dream Sports Mumbai Schools Sports Association tournament. The team secured a comfortable win.

stories.title: Antonio D'Silva football team secures victory
stories.summary: Dr. Antonio D'Silva High School defeated Rustomjee Cambridge International 4-0 in the Boys Under-12 football tournament at the MSSA ground. Arnav Rane and Kabir Sugnani each scored two goals for their respective sides in separate matches, while other teams recorded draws or wins in the division two clash.

stories.title: DPS-Modern Indian School marks 26th anniversary
stories.summary: DPS-Modern Indian School in Doha celebrated its 26th Annual Day with a theatrical production titled Anvay. The event featured addresses from school leadership and the Indian embassy, focusing on the institution's history and its commitment to nurturing creative and well-rounded individuals for future contributions to society.

stories.title: Anantha Lakshmi students qualify for state swimming
stories.summary: Eight students from Anantha Lakshmi International School have qualified for state-level swimming competitions following their performance at the district level. The students competed in various freestyle, backstroke, and butterfly events under the School Games Federation. The school chairman acknowledged the students for their success in the district trials.

stories.title: Green Institute opens fellowship applications
stories.summary: The Green Institute is accepting applications for its 2026-2027 fellowship program for sustainability advocates aged 18 to 35. Participants will develop climate advocacy skills and establish environmental clubs. The program includes a conditional $1,000 award for the post-fellowship period. Applications close on January 7, 2027.

stories.title: Asia House opens fellowship applications
stories.summary: Asia House is accepting applications for its 2027-2028 fellowship, which provides a £24,000 stipend. Two candidates will be selected to conduct 12 months of research on issues affecting Asia and the Middle East. The resulting work will be distributed to the organization's network of business and policy figures.

stories.title: Burlington students receive MROO scholarships
stories.summary: Five Burlington students have received $3,000 scholarships from the Municipal Retirees Organization Ontario. The awards are granted based on leadership and volunteer experience. To be eligible, recipients must be family members of current organization members. The program distributed $135,000 in total funding to students across the province.

stories.title: Helena graduate receives P.E.O. scholarship
stories.summary: Ashlyn Grasmick, a 2026 graduate of Capital High School, was awarded a $2,500 P.E.O. STAR Scholarship. The national award recognizes women for leadership, academics, and community service. Grasmick was recommended for the scholarship by the local Helena P.E.O. chapter, which identified her potential for future success.

stories.title: TiE Boston funds entrepreneurship scholarships
stories.summary: TiE Boston has partnered with METCO to provide $16,800 in scholarships for high school students. The funding covers tuition for seven students to attend the eight-month TYE Academy, which offers business education and mentorship. The partnership aims to expand access to entrepreneurship training for the 2026-2027 academic year.

stories.title: McLennan Community College awards record scholarships
stories.summary: The McLennan Community College Foundation awarded $925,069 in scholarships for the 2026-27 academic year. The funding supported 683 student awards, marking the largest amount in the foundation's 36-year history. The foundation also provided $208,000 in additional support through emergency grants to students on campus.

stories.title: Boca Grande Woman’s Club opens scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Boca Grande Woman’s Club is accepting applications for its four-year scholarship program until February 1, 2027. Applicants must have a weighted grade point average above 3.0 and be enrolled in post-secondary education. The club currently supports 49 students through this long-running scholarship initiative.

stories.title: University of Galway awards excellence scholarships
stories.summary: Cian Noland and Ciara Loftus, former students of Davitt College, have received excellence scholarships from the University of Galway. The awards recognize high academic achievement in the 2026 Leaving Certificate. The university presents these scholarships to some of the highest-achieving students entering the institution each year.

stories.title: Bosworth Independent School offers sixth form scholarships
stories.summary: Bosworth Independent School is offering four remaining 100% scholarships for A-level studies starting in September 2027. The program is open to British or dual-nationality students in Northamptonshire who demonstrate academic excellence. One of the five original scholarships has already been allocated to a successful applicant.

JEE Main 2027 registration window nears close
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency is closing registration for JEE Main 2027 Session 1 today. Around 11,19,062 candidates have paid the registration fee so far. Students who passed Class 12 in 2025 or 2026, or are appearing for the qualifying examination in 2027, remain eligible to apply.

IIT Madras sets GATE 2027 exam schedule
stories.summary: IIT Madras will conduct the GATE 2027 examination over six days in February 2027. The exams will take place in two daily sessions, forenoon and afternoon, across 30 papers. The branch-wise schedule is currently being finalised for release on the official website.

stories.title: BSEB releases second dummy admit cards for 2027 exams
stories.summary: The Bihar School Examination Board has released second dummy admit cards for Matric and Intermediate students. Candidates have until November 26 to report discrepancies through their school or college principals. Corrections are being handled via dedicated email addresses for each examination level.

stories.title: SUNY reports drop in international student enrollment
stories.summary: SUNY saw a 1.3 percent increase in overall enrollment between the 2025 and 2026 fall semesters. Despite this, the system recorded an 8.7 percent decrease in international students, including a 22 percent decline at the graduate level. Federal policy changes are cited as a potential deterrent.

stories.title: Irish universities report 8 million euro loss from visa refusals
stories.summary: Four Irish universities lost over 8 million euro in tuition fees for the 2026/27 academic year due to an increase in international student visa refusals. The Department of Justice maintains that its criteria for granting such visas have remained unchanged throughout the period.

stories.title: UK clarifies financial exemptions for student visa applicants
stories.summary: The UK government confirmed that two categories of international student visa applicants are exempt from proving they can financially support themselves. The exemptions are based on residency status and specific roles within a university. The guidance is currently being noted by prospective students.

stories.title: UK confirms financial proof exemptions for some foreign students
stories.summary: The UK government has confirmed that certain international students are not required to demonstrate financial support when applying for a student visa. The exemption applies to two categories based on residency history or university roles. The update is currently being reviewed by prospective applicants.

Federal court strikes down fixed stay limits for non-immigrant visas
stories.summary: A federal district court in Massachusetts ruled against Department of Homeland Security regulations that sought to impose fixed stay limits on F, J, and I visa holders. The court found the rule violated the Administrative Procedure Act and Congress's original intent for the programs.

stories.title: Google to invest 5 million dollars in IIT Kharagpur
stories.summary: Google announced a 5 million dollar investment in IIT Kharagpur to support research in artificial intelligence. The funding targets the deployment of AI models for Indic languages, agriculture, materials science, and educational technology. The company says it is excited to help accelerate this work.

stories.title: Google funds AI research at IIT Kharagpur
stories.summary: Google is providing USD 5 million to the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur to support AI research in fields including agriculture and materials science. The funding aims to accelerate AI development and build technical talent in India. The company says the partnership will also expand AI training opportunities.

stories.title: Assam to train 20,000 teachers in AI literacy
stories.summary: Assam is launching an AI training programme for 20,000 teachers in partnership with IIT Madras. The initiative, implemented by Samagra Shiksha Asom, focuses on integrating AI tools into lesson planning and assessment design. The training will be delivered in two phases, with 10,000 teachers participating in each round.

stories.title: UMass Dartmouth targets AI literacy for Class of 2028
stories.summary: The University of Massachusetts Dartmouth is integrating AI into its undergraduate curriculum, funding 16 courses and a campus framework. Provost Ramprasad Balasubramanian identified a goal for the Class of 2028 to graduate fully AI literate. The university aims to connect critical evaluation with practical skills for future careers.

stories.title: Google.org commits C$7 million to youth AI literacy
stories.summary: Google.org is committing over C$7 million to AI-education efforts in Canada, with a goal to reach 300,000 young people by 2028. The package includes training for 7,000 educators through the Raspberry Pi Foundation. These figures are projections, as the initiative builds on existing programs to expand its reach.

stories.title: UGC chairman calls for responsible, ethical use of AI in education - New Age BD
Ghana prepares for National Education Week
stories.summary: As Ghana approaches National Education Week, discussions are centering on the role of artificial intelligence in the classroom. The country is evaluating how emerging technology can improve learning outcomes and support teachers. The focus remains on ensuring digital competence and critical thinking skills for the future workforce.

stories.title: Africa Teacher Development and EdTech Summit to examine AI’s impact on education - Business News Nigeria
Africa Teacher Development Summit to be held virtually
stories.summary: The Africa Teacher Development and EdTech Summit is scheduled for November 28. The virtual event aims to bring together policymakers and innovators to discuss transforming education and strengthening teacher capacity. The summit is organised by TrainDTrainer, an education development organisation founded by Dr. Onyekachi Onwudike-Jumbo.

stories.title: Edo state government encourages teacher professional development
stories.summary: The Edo state government has urged teachers to adopt new technologies and innovative methods to improve student learning. Commissioner for Education Dr. Washington Osifo stated that teachers are central to the successful implementation of educational reforms. The call was made during a conference for private school owners and teachers.

stories.title: Kwara trains Arabic and Islamic school teachers
stories.summary: The Kwara State Government has completed a two-day training workshop for teachers in Arabic and Islamic schools. The programme covered modern teaching methods, digital literacy, and financial skills. Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq stated that the administration is committed to improving education quality across all sectors in the state.

stories.title: DepEd earns high satisfaction rating in SWS survey
stories.summary: The Department of Education received a net satisfaction rating of +61 for public education in a recent Social Weather Stations survey. Secretary Sonny Angara credited teachers for the result and announced a laptop distribution programme. The department aims to continue reforms and provide support for career advancement.

stories.title: DepEd distributes MacBook Neo laptops in Antipolo
stories.summary: The Department of Education has distributed 1,441 MacBook Neo laptops to teachers in Antipolo City. This rollout is part of a national computerisation programme that aims to provide over 230,000 units to public school teachers. The department has also procured additional devices for its administrative personnel.

stories.title: Teacher agency key to implementing government reforms to report - Schools Week
South Africa to update teacher training for AI
stories.summary: The Department of Higher Education and Training plans to introduce a revised policy in 2027 to incorporate AI into national teacher-training standards. The update aligns with the Higher Education Qualifications Sub-Framework. The shift aims to address the impact of artificial intelligence on teaching, assessment, and academic integrity.

stories.title: Kiran Bedi named national mentor for teachers
stories.summary: The National Council for Teacher Education has appointed former IPS officer Kiran Bedi as a national mentor under its MITRA-NMM initiative. Bedi will share her administrative and leadership experience with teachers across India. The appointment was formalised during an online session held on November 18.

stories.title: CBSE directs schools to mark Constitution Day
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has instructed affiliated schools to hold activities for Constitution Day on November 26. Suggested programmes include reading the Preamble and hosting poster-making competitions. The board aims to encourage students to engage with the history and values of the Indian Constitution.

stories.title: CBSE plans shift toward practical assessment
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education is preparing to revise its assessment system for Classes 10 and 12. The proposed approach will prioritise conceptual understanding and practical application over rote memorisation. The board says the changes are being aligned with the National Education Policy.

stories.title: Dallas ISD to close 6 schools due to deficit
stories.summary: Dallas ISD will close six schools as it manages a $128 million budget deficit. The district reported an enrollment of 3,099 students fewer than projected for the current school year. The move follows broader trends of declining student enrollment across the state of Texas.

stories.title: School nurse group calls for measles prevention
stories.summary: The National Association of School Nurses is urging action as the United States loses its measles elimination status. The call follows a doubling of cases across the country. The association is focusing on prevention and response strategies to address the rising health concerns in school environments.

stories.title: Madison school district adds IB program
stories.summary: Nuestro Mundo has become the first public elementary school in Dane County to offer the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme. The school completed two years as a candidate before receiving official authorization this fall. The designation expands the district's available curriculum options for local families.

stories.title: Colton board requests climate education campaign
stories.summary: The Colton Town Board has adopted a resolution calling on the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation to launch a statewide educational campaign on extreme climate worsening. The board approved the measure during its October 21 meeting to address concerns regarding environmental changes.

stories.title: Centre signs agreements to upgrade Telangana ITI clusters
stories.summary: The government has signed agreements with four industry partners to upgrade Industrial Training Institute clusters in Telangana. The project involves an investment of 1,011 crore rupees under the PM-SETU scheme. The initiative aims to provide sector-specific expertise in areas including manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and defence electronics.

stories.title: UGC flags 32 fake universities
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission has listed 32 institutions as fake universities, with Delhi hosting 12 of them. Eighteen of the names appeared on a similar list in 2023. The regulator has urged families to verify the legal status of institutions before committing to any academic program.

stories.title: Applications open for 2027 Funza Lushaka bursary
stories.summary: The Funza Lushaka Bursary Scheme is accepting applications until January 31, 2027. The program, a collaboration between the Department of Basic Education and other national bodies, offers financial aid to students pursuing teaching careers. It is described as a nation-building mission to shape future classrooms.

stories.title: Medical commission investigates ragging in Rajasthan
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has demanded a response from a Rajasthan government medical college following allegations of ragging. First-year students reported being subjected to degrading acts and social exclusion by seniors. The commission warned that denials without evidence would not be accepted by its anti-ragging cell.

stories.title: Medical seats remain vacant despite high demand
stories.summary: Over 3,000 MBBS seats remained unfilled following NEET-UG 2026 counselling rounds. While government college seats were fully occupied, vacancies persisted in deemed universities, particularly in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Puducherry. The trend has raised questions regarding high tuition fees and equitable access to medical education.

stories.title: NMC proposes change to foreign medical graduate rules
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has proposed removing the requirement that foreign medical graduates hold a licence at par with citizens of the country where they studied. Candidates would instead need registration with the local professional regulatory body. The draft amendment aims to address current eligibility debates.

stories.title: Court allows student to retain medical seat
stories.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed the National Testing Agency's decision to withhold a student's NEET re-examination result. The agency had cited an alleged mobile phone infraction during a previously cancelled test. The court noted that the initial exam results were rendered inconsequential by the cancellation.

CLAT 2027 admit cards available for download
stories.summary: The Consortium of National Law Universities has released admit cards for the 2027 undergraduate and postgraduate entrance exams. Candidates must access the portal to download their hall tickets before the December 6 examination date. The window for retrieval is now open until the morning of the test.

stories.title: NNPC and TotalEnergies open scholarship applications
stories.summary: NNPC Limited and TotalEnergies are accepting applications for fully funded Master’s degree scholarships in France for Nigerian graduates. The programme aims to support talented students pursuing advanced education in strategically important academic disciplines. Successful applicants receive full-board coverage for their postgraduate studies.

stories.title: University of Leeds offers 21 PhD scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Leeds is inviting applications for up to 21 PhD Excellence Scholarships for the 2027/28 academic year. These awards provide full tuition fee coverage for doctoral students in business, management, economics, and finance. The number of final awards remains subject to the quality of applications received.

stories.title: New Zealand PhD programme offers NZ$45,000 stipend
stories.summary: The Ag Emissions Centre in New Zealand is offering five PhD scholarships for research into reducing agricultural greenhouse gas emissions. The programme provides a tax-free annual stipend of NZ$45,000 alongside tuition coverage. The research aims to develop practical solutions for methane and nitrous oxide reduction.

stories.title: KAUST opens postgraduate applications for Pakistani students
stories.summary: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology is accepting applications for its Fall 2027 Master’s and PhD programmes. The KAUST Fellowship provides admitted students with coverage for tuition, accommodation, health insurance, and living expenses. The university aims to remove the main costs associated with postgraduate study.

stories.title: Clements-Archer fellowship opens for UT Austin graduates
stories.summary: Applications are open for the 2027-2028 Clements-Archer National Security Policy Postdoctoral Fellowship. The two-year programme provides an $80,000 stipend for recent PhD graduates from the University of Texas at Austin to work in Washington, D.C. Fellows must maintain full-time residence in the city throughout the term.

stories.title: Cambridge opens Mastercard Foundation scholarship applications
stories.summary: The University of Cambridge is accepting applications for the 2027/2028 Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program. The initiative targets young African students focused on climate resilience and sustainability. The programme aims to enable talented individuals to pursue master’s degrees and grow their leadership potential.

stories.title: Dataphyte Foundation launches investigative media fellowship
stories.summary: The Dataphyte Foundation is inviting Nigerian journalists to apply for a two-month investigative fellowship focused on foreign-funded infrastructure projects. The programme will train five participants to report on Official Development Assistance and public-private partnerships. Applications for the Infra-Watch Media Fellowship close on November 27.

stories.title: NAPB-APBA Borlaug scholarship offers six PhD awards
stories.summary: The NAPB Borlaug Scholars-Africa Programme is offering six awards to African PhD students in plant breeding. The scholarship provides financial support, international exposure, and professional mentorship over two years. The programme aims to nurture the next generation of scientists through research networking and academic funding.

stories.title: COMSATS University ranks in global sustainability top 500
stories.summary: COMSATS University Islamabad has secured the second position among Pakistani universities in the QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2027. The institution placed joint 477th globally with an overall score of 72.7. It leads the country in environmental research and health and wellbeing indicators.

stories.title: National University of Singapore rises in science rankings
stories.summary: The National University of Singapore has moved to second place in a global interdisciplinary science ranking, surpassing Stanford. MIT retained the top position in the table, which assesses research funding and support across 102 countries. This marks the first time a non-U.S. university has reached the top two.

stories.title: Galgotias University Rises 32 Places in QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, in a Year When Most Indian Universities
NUS overtakes Stanford in global science table
stories.summary: The National University of Singapore climbed to second place in the latest Times Higher Education science ranking, scoring 88.5 points. The institution finished ahead of Stanford’s 88 points, while MIT remained first with 89.5. It is the first time a university other than MIT or Stanford has placed top two.

stories.title: UK and EU discuss student mobility and fees
stories.summary: UK and EU officials met on November 20 to discuss post-Brexit migration and education ties. The talks included a proposal for a Youth Experience Scheme for 100,000 young people. Discussions regarding reduced tuition fees for students remain ongoing, with no immediate changes to existing policies.

stories.title: UK and EU agree on youth mobility scheme
stories.summary: The UK and EU have agreed to a Youth Experience Scheme allowing 100,000 young people from each side to reside, study, and work in the other's territory for three years. A decision on reduced tuition fees for students has been delayed, prompting concerns regarding university finances.

stories.title: Tuition fee decision delayed in UK-EU reset talks
stories.summary: The UK and EU have committed to finding ways to increase study opportunities following recent Brexit talks. A decision on lowering tuition fees has been pushed back by six months. The two sides have agreed to work toward a supplementing agreement regarding costs for international students.

stories.title: Universities UK supports new mobility agreement
stories.summary: Universities UK has welcomed the new mobility deal between the UK and EU, which aims to increase study opportunities. While tuition fee reductions were not included in the current agreement, officials have indicated that discussions on the matter will continue over the next six months.
